verdicts.claim: PH retired the hunter auto-notification boost; makers self-submit with no algorithmic advantage from a hunter; ranking is a composite of upvotes/hour, comment depth, CTR, and share activity rather than raw early spike.
verdicts.evidence: Cited source (hub.causo.ai/guides/product-hunt-launch-2026-realistic-playbook) does say the hunter auto-notify lever is 'gone' and the boost is 'no longer a meaningful ranking input,' and this is echoed by several independent third-party guides (foundra.ai, arc.dev) describing self-hunting as now standard — that part is reasonably well corroborated by consensus, though still all secondary/unofficial reporting. But the specific composite-ranking formula is NOT confirmable: Product Hunt's own official Help Center (help.producthunt.com/en/articles/10275873-what-are-points) only says points reflect 'genuine engagement, including upvotes and other signals, such as comments' — no mention of upvotes/hour, CTR, or share activity. Worse, another independent guide found via search directly contradicts the claim's 'rather than raw early spike' framing: it says the algorithm 'weighs early-hour velocity ... heavily' and that '30 upvotes in the first hour ... outranks 200 upvotes spread across the day.' Product Hunt does not publish its algorithm, and third-party accounts disagree on the details, so the specific mechanics in this claim cannot be confirmed.

verdicts.claim: A #8-of-day SaaS reporting tool got 564 visitors and 56 signups; a top-50 AI knowledge tool got zero signups and the founder concluded PH is 'awareness, not acquisition.' (single cited source: indiehackers.com/post/...-77b1fc59e4)
verdicts.evidence: Both underlying facts are real and independently verifiable, but NOT from the single URL cited. The zero-signups/top-50/'awareness, not acquisition' quote is confirmed verbatim at the cited URL (MinervaAI, an AI Obsidian knowledge tool: 'Product Hunt and directories are awareness, not acquisition.'). The 564 visitors / 56 signups / #8-of-day figures are real but come from a DIFFERENT, uncited Indie Hackers post: https://www.indiehackers.com/post/aftermath-of-our-disappointing-product-hunt-launch-a81fea3a52 (product 'Raport,' a reporting tool; exact text: '564 Visits from PH (25th + 26th January)... 56 signups... we ended up being #8 product of the day,' dated Jan 2022). Flag: the research lane cited only one source URL for both data points, but that source only supports the second half of the claim; the first half needs its own citation to the 2022 Raport post.

verdicts.claim: Product Hunt links pass no SEO authority (rel=ugc); pair with permanent indexed directories for lasting value.
verdicts.evidence: Verified independently by fetching live HTML, not just trusting the cited blog. curl of a real Product Hunt product page (producthunt.com/products/claude-code) shows the outbound 'Visit website' button and maker links carry rel="noreferrer noopener ugc" (data-test="visit-website-button"). Per Google's own documentation, ugc/nofollow-class rel values are hints Google generally excludes from passing ranking signals, matching the claim's 'no SEO authority' framing. The cited puthusu.com blog's paraphrase matches this primary-source finding, though note puthusu.com is itself pitching its own competing directory as the 'permanent indexed' alternative, so treat the specific recommendation (not just the technical rel=ugc fact) as promotional.

verdicts.claim: Kicktraq's sponsorship/advertising program is currently paused, with no live pricing or intake.
verdicts.evidence: Fetched https://www.kicktraq.com/sponsors/ directly (fresh, not cached). Page currently states: 'We are currently pausing advertising on Kicktraq in preparation for changes coming soon.' No pricing table or intake form present. Matches the claim exactly.

verdicts.claim: PH's own readiness screening reportedly tells ~70% of inquiring founders they're not ready, with enterprise-leaning buyer or lack of self-serve onboarding as primary disqualifiers.
verdicts.evidence: The 70% figure is real but is NOT Product Hunt's own screening — the claim misattributes it. Traced to its origin: Lenny's Newsletter (https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/how-to-successfully-launch-on-product), which quotes Leo Bosuener of the outside marketing agency Social Growth Labs: 'Every week our agency receives a dozen requests from founders looking for help launching on Product Hunt, and we convince 70% of them that they aren't ready.' This is a third-party paid launch-consulting agency's client-intake screening, not any process run by Product Hunt the platform/company. The intermediate cited source (hub.causo.ai) itself correctly attributes this to 'experienced launch consultants' — the claim as written ('PH's own readiness screening') introduces the misattribution. The self-serve-onboarding disqualifier is genuinely in the Lenny's piece ('you need a smooth, self-serve onboarding flow'); the 'enterprise buyer' disqualifier appears only in causo.ai's paraphrase, not verified verbatim in the Lenny's primary source.
verdicts.corrected: The ~70% 'not ready' figure comes from an outside Product Hunt launch-consulting agency (Social Growth Labs, via Lenny's Newsletter), screening its own paying clients — not from any readiness screening run by Product Hunt itself. Product Hunt has no known official readiness-screening process. Self-serve onboarding as a disqualifier is confirmed in the primary source; the enterprise-buyer disqualifier is an unverified paraphrase.

verdicts.claim: Shopify's 2026 App Store requires GraphQL Admin API only (REST legacy), GDPR webhooks, Shopify App Pricing billing, and a 2-4 week review, so it's not a same-sprint option.
verdicts.evidence: GraphQL-only and REST-legacy confirmed verbatim on the cited page (shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/app-store-requirements): 'As of April 1, 2025 all new public apps must be built exclusively with the GraphQL Admin API' and 'As of October 1, 2024 the REST Admin API is considered a legacy API and should no longer be used.' Shopify App Pricing/Billing API requirement also confirmed verbatim on that page. GDPR webhooks and the review-timeline figure are NOT on that specific page but are confirmed on other official/primary Shopify sources per instructions to check alternates: Shopify's compliance docs (shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/compliance/privacy-law-compliance) and Shopify Community threads confirm all public apps must subscribe to mandatory GDPR compliance webhooks or be rejected on submission, regardless of whether the app stores personal data. Review timeline: Shopify's own review-process doc plus multiple community reports converge on roughly 1-2 weeks official guideline extending to 2-4+ weeks in practice (some reports of 3-5+ weeks), so '2-4 week review' is a reasonable/defensible characterization, not an outlier claim. Net: every individual fact checks out against Shopify's own documentation ecosystem, just spread across multiple pages rather than the single cited URL — the 'not a same-sprint option' conclusion holds.
